cases.purpose: Three-peer roster convergence, leave propagation, heartbeat refresh against silent peer expiry (documented three deadlines), and leaf disconnection after seed loss.
cases.oracle: Independent protocol oracle. Persistent candidate shells run the UNCHANGED builtin as uid 2000 in private state directories on IPv4 loopback inside the disposable VM. The wire format (1212-byte datagram, BCLSTR2 magic, big-endian port, 32-row table, keyed BLAKE2b-256 over the first 1180 bytes) is the fixture's own implementation on hashlib, validated in setup against BLAKE2b known answers and round trips; oracle peers, probes and decoys are owned UDP sockets that validate every request field by field. Expected values never come from candidate output alone: identities and rosters are cross-checked on the wire (authenticated PONG and ROSTER packets), file contents are parsed independently, timing bounds come from the documented deadline (request deadline, heartbeat every quarter, expiry after three), and kernel facts come from /proc (process tree, UDP table, receive queues), inotify, bind() collisions, modes and owners. Setup controls (a failure is an ERROR, never a candidate result): hashing and codec known answers, loopback delivery of 0/1/1212/65507 byte datagrams, the UDP table and its queues, wildcard decoys, every oracle peer mode, inotify atomicity detection, and the persistent-shell driver (status/stdout/stderr extraction, deadline kill, removal of a child that outlives its shell, reaping). Only processes started by the fixture are signaled; every key is evaluated for every vector, an unevaluated key prints ERROR, and any control or fixture exception prints CONTROL-INVALID and exits 97.
cases.comparison: Every key of every vector is evaluated and must be yes. [three-peer-convergence] joins-ok: the seed and two peers started and joined; identities-on-wire: each PONG gives the node id and port, one cluster id, three distinct nodes; rosters-converge: all three members files equal the wire-derived list (seed, peer, peer) within 5 s; members-commands-agree: cluster members prints the same list on each; c-left-status: the third peer leave exits 0; leave-removed-everywhere: the seed and the other peer drop it within 4 s; survivors-intact: both survivors keep their listeners and state=initialized; c-state-cleaned: the leaver state files are gone. [expiry-and-refresh] oracles-joined: two oracle nodes joined the seed next to two candidate peers; silent-expires-not-early: the oracle that never beats leaves the roster no earlier than three deadlines after its join (1.2 s); silent-expires-in-bound: and within three deadlines plus a quarter deadline plus 1.5 s; beating-oracle-retained: the oracle beating every half deadline outlives the silent one by more than two deadlines; beating-peers-retained: the two candidate peers stay in the seed roster at every poll; retention-ends-after-last-beat: the beating oracle expires three deadlines (within the slack) after its last heartbeat; expiry-propagates-to-peers: both candidate peers drop both oracles within 2 s. [seed-loss] peers-joined: seed and leaf joined with equal rosters; seed-left-status: the seed leave exits 0; leaf-disconnected: the leaf state file and status become disconnected within three deadlines plus slack; leaf-roster-self-only: the leaf roster keeps only itself; leaf-listener-alive: the leaf listener is alive; leaf-stopped-after-kill: after SIGKILL of the verified leaf listener, status reports stopped. Retained in the case tree: observations.jsonl (every command with its raw stdout, stderr, status, duration and finish time, every oracle exchange as hex, teardown findings, and r2 trace: the ordered observation timeline per vector - every datagram sent and received as hex with the source port, every peer verdict, inotify events, /proc process and UDP table observations, bind probes, directory snapshots, file contents read, kills, sentinel states, and every key evaluation interleaved with the observations that produced it) and the state directories themselves; the setup report is the stdout of the setup step.
